text:
alex: Heads-up — after landing the soft-lease handover we saw sporadic +80ms tails on small requests.

maria: Do you have a trace? is this during prefetch/eviction or while the batch is moving?

alex: trace: https://goto/trace/abc123 — looks like an inflight batch is held while lease transfer completes. you can see worker A waiting on worker B to ack.

devon: this rings a bell. the current queue contract basically assumes instant transfer of batch ownership. we never model a 'split in-flight' case where some requests keep referencing the same KV view while others move.

sophie: thinking out loud: introduce a tiny "handoff_token" in batch metadata. workers can continue serving requests that are read-only while token pending, but mutate/evict ops are gated until claim completes.

jay: that will help correctness but complicates eviction paths. also our telemetry doesn't surface 'handoff latency' today — we need a histogram for handoff_ms by tenant and model.

alex: :thumbsup: agree on telemetry. without that we can't tell if this is rare or systemic.

devon: RFC follow-up question: do we want synchronous handoff (block until claim) or eventual (grant temporary dual-read permission)? tradeoff: sync prevents double-exec but increases p99; eventual keeps latency low but harder correctness.

sophie: API sketch: enqueue() returns lease_id; worker.claim(lease_id) -> {ok, fallback_reason}. fallback must be able to drain the remaining batch and re-enqueue safely.

maria: edgecase: claim might race with prefetch eviction. if fallback triggers re-enqueue we could reorder requests and break per-tenant ordering guarantees.

devon: we already attach ordering hints per-request. proposal: keep strict FIFO only for small low-latency requests (<32 tokens). bulk/long requests are best-effort ordering. that limits visible reordering impact.

alex: proposal: land handoff_token, add metric handoff_ms, and canary for 48h. rollback plan: if handoff_ms_p99 > 50ms or user-facing error rate rises, revert to hard pinning for small requests.

jay: mitigation idea: fast-path bypass for tight-deadline requests (deadline_hint < 30ms) — skip handoff and serve locally. combine with admission credits so we don't overload the local fast-path.

sophie: yes — local fast-path + admission credits. make sure telemetry tags fast-path traces so we can compare quality.

maria: i'll add entries to the ops runbook: how to read handoff_ms, what to do when p99 crosses thresholds, how to interpret canary signals.

devon: another operational corner: rolling restarts. workers with pending handoffs should publish their inflight sets to control plane before draining so the replacement can claim gracefully.

alex: agreed. i'll draft a tiny proto change for batch metadata. pseudocode:```json
{
  "batch_id": "uuid",
  "lease_id": "uuid",
  "handoff_state": "PENDING|CLAIMED|FAILED",
  "deadline_hint_ms": 25
}
```

alex: putting a draft PR: https://git/repo/pr/4567 (proto + metric + safeguard flags)

jay: assigning the canary to eu-west-1 dedicated pool. i'll wire an alert: handoff_ms_p99 > 50ms -> paged.

sophie: also add an explainability tag to traces for "handoff" so SRE can quickly filter during incidents.

devon: if anyone's free later we can do a 30m pairing to wire the metric and eviction hook.

maria: i can join at 3pm PT.

alex: thanks all — i'll keep the thread open for RFC comments and will post the PR when ready.
